intro: Every state runs its own economic-development incentives on top of federal programs — tax credits, seed funds, deal-closing grants, training reimbursements and more. State incentives stack with federal ones. This is a starter set covering 12 states; the rest are listed with their official portal on the State Portals page and are being backfilled over time.

states.period: Ongoing, three application periods per year
states.nodalAgency: Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)
states.summary: An income tax credit for businesses that want to locate or grow in California, awarded competitively based on jobs created, investment, and strategic importance. FY2025-26 allocation is $215 million statewide.

schemes.name: California Competes Tax Credit
schemes.benefit: Negotiated multi-year income tax credit; $215M allocated statewide for FY2025-26
schemes.description: Competitive tax credit based on a 5-year agreement tied to job-creation, salary, and investment milestones.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses of any size or industry planning to locate, stay, or grow in California

states.summary: Refundable tax credits for firms in targeted industries (finance, tech, manufacturing, agriculture and more) that create jobs or make significant capital investment in New York.

schemes.name: Excelsior Jobs Program
schemes.benefit: Up to 5 refundable tax credits over up to 10 years (jobs, investment, R&D, real property, child care)
schemes.description: Jobs Tax Credit up to 6.85% of wages per net new job; Investment Tax Credit at 2% of qualified investment; R&D credit up to 50% of the federal R&D credit claimed in NY.
schemes.eligibility: Firms in targeted industries creating/maintaining new jobs or making significant investment

states.nodalAgency: Office of the Governor, Economic Development & Tourism
states.summary: The largest state 'deal-closing' fund in the nation, awarding performance-based grants to companies choosing a Texas site over an out-of-state competitor.

schemes.name: Texas Enterprise Fund
schemes.benefit: Negotiated deal-closing grant, sized by an analytical model based on jobs, timeline and wages
schemes.description: Performance-based grant requiring unanimous approval from the Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Speaker of the House, with clawback provisions if job/wage commitments aren't met.
schemes.eligibility: Well-established, financially sound businesses in advanced industries with a competing out-of-state site

states.policy: MassVentures START Program & Early Stage Fund
states.summary: Non-dilutive funding for Massachusetts companies commercializing SBIR/STTR Phase II technology, plus direct seed-stage equity investment.

schemes.name: START Program
schemes.description: For companies that have received a federal SBIR/STTR Phase II award; covers commercialization activities not funded by the federal grant. $41.7M awarded to 141 companies since 2012.
schemes.eligibility: Massachusetts-based companies with a Phase II SBIR/STTR award

schemes.name: Early Stage Fund
schemes.description: Direct equity investment in Massachusetts seed-stage deep-tech companies, with potential for follow-on funding.

states.nodalAgency: PA Department of Community & Economic Development (via the Ben Franklin Technology Development Authority)
states.summary: Pennsylvania's statewide innovation network providing early-stage funding and hands-on support through four regional partner organizations.

schemes.name: Ben Franklin Technology Partners funding
schemes.benefit: Up to $500,000 for tech startups (series of investments); up to $250,000 for existing manufacturers
schemes.description: Early-stage investment plus expert guidance and strategic partnerships, delivered through regional Ben Franklin offices covering the whole state.

states.summary: Non-dilutive seed grants for early-stage North Carolina startups with a proven concept, running since 2006.

schemes.name: NC IDEA SEED Grant
schemes.description: Milestone-based grant over 6-12 months for startups with a demonstrated proof of concept and MVP; over $10.3M awarded to 225+ companies since 2006.
schemes.eligibility: At least one full-time founder living in North Carolina; proven concept, not yet profitable

states.summary: Maryland's leading source of funding for early-stage, technology-based businesses, with a portfolio of 400+ seed investments since 1998.

schemes.name: TEDCO Seed Investment Fund
schemes.benefit: Seed-stage investment; amount varies by deal
schemes.description: Targets Maryland companies with fewer than 20 employees, generally under 5 years old, developing and commercializing new technology-based products.
schemes.eligibility: Maryland principal place of business; at least one full-time employee

states.nodalAgency: Michigan Strategic Fund / Michigan Economic Development Corporation (MEDC)
states.summary: Performance-based grants (with some loan/other-support options) for businesses creating jobs or making qualified investment in Michigan.

schemes.name: Michigan Business Development Program
schemes.benefit: Negotiated performance-based grant with flexible terms; may include repayment provisions
schemes.description: Preference given to businesses choosing to locate or expand in Michigan over an out-of-state alternative.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses creating qualified new jobs and/or making qualified new investment in Michigan

states.nodalAgency: Governor's Office of Workforce Transformation / Ohio Department of Development
states.summary: Reimburses Ohio employers for the cost of short-term, technology-focused credentials for current and future employees.

schemes.name: TechCred
schemes.benefit: Up to $1,000 per employee per credential, max $30,000 per application period
schemes.description: Reimburses training costs for short-term, industry-recognized, tech-focused credentials (IT, cybersecurity, robotics/automation, and more) completed within a year.
schemes.eligibility: Ohio employers, using a training provider from the state's eligible-provider list

states.period: Annual application cycles (e.g. Proof of Concept due Aug 27, 2026)
states.nodalAgency: Colorado Office of Economic Development & International Trade (OEDIT)
states.summary: State grants supporting Colorado's advanced-industry startups and research institutions across four grant tracks.

schemes.name: Advanced Industries Proof of Concept Grant
schemes.description: Helps Colorado research institutions speed up applied research and commercialize it with private-sector partners.
schemes.eligibility: Colorado research institutions and their commercialization partners

schemes.name: Advanced Industries Early-Stage Capital and Retention Grant
schemes.description: Helps Colorado-based advanced-industries companies develop and commercialize technologies created or manufactured in-state.

states.policy: Virginia Innovation Partnership Corporation (VIPC) funding programs
states.nodalAgency: Virginia Innovation Partnership Corporation (nonprofit arm of VIPA)
states.summary: Virginia's commercialization and seed-stage economic-development driver, running multiple grant and direct-investment programs for early-stage companies.

schemes.name: Launch Program
schemes.benefit: Non-dilutive grants and dilutive convertible notes
schemes.description: For high-potential, pre-MVP Virginia startups that have raised minimal equity and generated limited revenue.
schemes.eligibility: Pre-MVP Virginia startups with strong potential economic impact

schemes.name: Lab-to-Launch Initiative
schemes.description: For early-stage Virginia startups using a Fast-Track License Agreement with one of Virginia's six R1-designated universities.

schemes.name: Virginia Venture Partners (VVP)
schemes.description: VIPC's direct venture-capital investment platform for high-potential Virginia-based startups.
schemes.eligibility: Virginia-based startups with high growth potential

states.policy: Invest Georgia / Georgia Venture Capital Program
states.nodalAgency: Invest Georgia (state instrumentality) / Georgia Department of Community Affairs
states.summary: A state-backed fund-of-funds that invests as a limited partner in seed, venture-capital, and growth-equity funds targeting Georgia-based businesses.

schemes.name: Georgia Venture Capital Program
schemes.benefit: $30M SSBCI allocation deployed via participating VC funds
schemes.description: Invest Georgia invests as a limited partner in seed and early-stage VC funds, including funds targeting SEDI-owned businesses, which in turn invest in Georgia startups.
schemes.eligibility: Georgia-based businesses funded indirectly through participating venture-capital funds
